decision.explanation: The original documents D2S2 and D3S2 explicitly state that 'Egan Bernal officially won the 2019 Tour de France'. While D2S1 and D3S1 contain the name 'Tadej Pogačar' in the context of the same date, the specific claim of winning the 2019 Tour de France is attributed solely to Egan Bernal in the provided text segments. The mention of Tadej Pogačar in the source text (D2S1/D3S1) appears to be an error or a misattribution within the source itself, as the subsequent sentences (D2S2/D3S2) correctly identify Bernal as the winner. The instruction to treat all sources as fallible and not to invent authority means we must rely on the explicit assertion of the winner found in the text. Since both D2 and D3 assert Bernal as the winner, and neither asserts Pogačar as the winner (only mentioning his name in proximity), the only supported answer is Egan Bernal. The previous inclusion of Tadej Pogačar in R5 was likely due to a misreading of the source text where his name appeared near the winner's name, but the text does not claim he won.
